propositions.text: The claimant is a Mexican citizen seeking refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of Mexico, seeks refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the IRPA).

propositions.text: The claimant's identity was established by a certified copy of his passport.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity has been established through a certified copy of the claimant's passport.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant is a Mexican citizen seeking refugee protection and his identity was established by passport copy.

propositions.text: The claimant alleged that on a date in 2008, he was at his employer's office which had a company telephone.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that on XXXXX, 2008, sometime between 3:00-4:00 PM, he was at the office of the XXXXX XXXXX he worked for which XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX. The office has a company telephone.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he was at his employer's office in 2008, which had a company telephone.

propositions.text: The claimant saw three unknown men outside, two by a black pick-up truck without plates wearing dark glasses, and one knocking at the door.
propositions.quote: He heard a knock at the door. He looked out and saw three men, two of them standing beside a black pick-up truck without license plates and they were wearing dark glasses. The other man was standing at the door knocking. He did not know these men.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he saw three unknown men outside, two by a black pick-up truck and one knocking at the door.

propositions.text: The man knocking asked if this was the claimant's neighbour's home, got angry when told no, swore, threatened, and demanded entry; claimant refused.
propositions.quote: The claimant answered the door and the man standing there asked him if this was XXXXX XXXXX home, the claimant's neighbour. The claimant told him no and the man, who thought the claimant was lying, got angry and started to swear at him. The man threatened the claimant and demanded that he open the door and let him in. The claimant refused and the man went to the next door.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges the man knocking asked for his neighbour, got angry, threatened him, and demanded entry, which he refused.

propositions.text: The claimant saw the men dragging his neighbour into a car; one threatened him with a gun not to say anything; men fled with neighbour.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that he saw the three men dragging his neighbour and pushed him into the car. The claimant said the man who was knocking his door pulled out a gun and threatened him not to say anything or he would be killed. Other neigbours started to come out of their homes and the claimant alleged that the men sped off in their car with the neighbour.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he saw men drag his neighbour into a car, threatened with a gun, and fled with the neighbour.

propositions.text: The claimant said he phoned the police and reported the incident.
propositions.quote: The claimant said he phoned the police and made a report of the incident.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he reported the incident to the police by phone.

propositions.text: The claimant saw a newspaper article about human remains including his neighbour's and reported anonymously to police hotline what he observed.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX 2008, he saw an article in the newspaper that human remains were found in different places in the city and that one of them was his neighbour who he had witnessed being dragged from his home. The claimant alleged that he called the police hotline which is set up for anonymous callers to make confidential reports and reported what he had observed on XXXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he saw a newspaper about human remains including his neighbour's and reported anonymously to police hotline.

propositions.text: The claimant alleged he saw a kidnapper at his door, overheard a death threat on phone, and received a threatening note signed by XXXXX.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX, 2008, the claimant alleged that he heard a knock on his door and, peeking out, he saw a man he recognized as one of the kidnappers who had taken his neighbour away. The claimant also alleged that he overheard the man talking on his cell phone that he would kill the claimant, after which he slipped a note under the claimant's door. The note threatened to kill the claimant and that he should not contact the police. It was also signed by XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he saw a kidnapper at his door, overheard a death threat, and received a threatening note signed by XXXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant alleged he fled his area, job, and belongings due to threats, moved to two other locations but was found each time.
propositions.quote: Realizing he was being threatened by drug gangsters, the claimant further alleged that he left the area, his job and belongings and went to live in the city of XXXXX where he found a job. The claimant alleged that he was found and he moved to two other locations where he was also found.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he fled his area and job due to threats but was found at two other locations.

propositions.text: The claimant alleged he was denied a US visa, came to Canada on Feb 24, 2009, and filed for refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that he applied for a visa to the United States but was denied, so he came to Canada on February 24, 2009 and filed for refugee protection on XXXXX, 2009.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he was denied US visa, came to Canada in 2009, and filed refugee claim.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the IRPA.

propositions.text: The claimant lacks a well-founded fear of persecution for a Convention reason and removal to Mexico poses no personal risk to life or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: The claimant does not have a well-founded fear of persecution for a Convention reason and his removal to Mexico would not subject him personally to a risk to life, or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or a danger of torture.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee and removal to Mexico poses no personal risk.

propositions.text: The panel considered whether the claimant's fear is objectively reasonable, including state protection adequacy and claimant's efforts to seek it.
propositions.quote: In arriving at my decision, the panel considered the issue of whether the claimant's fear is objectively reasonable. In this regard, the panel considered whether or not there is adequate state protection in Mexico, whether the claimant took all reasonable steps to avail himself of that protection, and whether he has provided clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect.

paragraphs.summary: The panel considered if the claimant's fear is objectively reasonable, including state protection and claimant's efforts.

propositions.text: The Board is guided by Supreme Court and Federal Court cases on state protection principles.
propositions.quote: The Board, in assessing the issue of state protection, is guided by a number of cases from the Supreme Court of Canada and the Federal Court.

propositions.text: The panel applied these state protection principles to the claimant's case.
propositions.quote: The courts have established a number of principles relating to state protection and the panel has applied those principles to the case at hand.

paragraphs.summary: The panel applied Supreme Court and Federal Court principles on state protection to this case.

propositions.text: There is a presumption that states, except in complete breakdown, can protect their citizens.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that, except in situations where the state is in complete breakdown, the state is capable of protecting its citizens.

propositions.text: International protection applies only when a claimant has no other recourse available.
propositions.quote: The presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens underscores the principle that international protection comes into play only when a refugee claimant has no other recourse available.

paragraphs.summary: The panel states a presumption that states can protect citizens and international protection applies only when no other recourse exists.

propositions.text: Claimants must provide clear and convincing evidence that state protection is inadequate to rebut presumption of protection.
propositions.quote: A claimant who alleges that state protection is inadequate must persuade the Board that the evidence establishes that the state protection is inadequate. To rebut the presumption of state protection, a claimant must provide "clear and convincing" evidence of the state's inability to protect its citizens.

propositions.text: Evidence must be reliable, probative, and satisfy balance of probabilities that protection is inadequate.
propositions.quote: The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and probative, it must also satisfy the Board, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate.

propositions.text: State efforts to protect, even if not always successful, do not rebut presumption if state controls territory and authority.
propositions.quote: Where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authority in place and makes serious efforts to protect its citizens, the mere fact that the state's efforts are not always successful will not rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Subjective reluctance to engage state does not rebut presumption of protection in functioning democracy.
propositions.quote: A claimant cannot rebut the presumption of state protection in a functioning democracy by asserting only a subjective reluctance to engage the state.

propositions.text: Doubting protection effectiveness without testing it does not rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: Doubting the effectiveness of the protection offered by the state when one has not really tested it does not rebut the existence of a presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel explains the high evidentiary standard to rebut presumption of state protection in functioning democracies.

propositions.text: Refugee protection is surrogate, invoked only after unsuccessful state protection attempts.
propositions.quote: Refugee protection is meant to be a form of surrogate protection to be invoked only in those situations where the refugee claimant has unsuccessfully sought the protections of his home state.

propositions.text: Claimant must approach state for protection when reasonably available; failure to do so usually fatal to claim in functioning democracy.
propositions.quote: The onus is on the claimant to approach the state for protection in situations where state protection might be reasonably forthcoming. In the absence of a compelling explanation, a failure to pursue state protection opportunities within the home state will usually be fatal to a refugee claim, at least where the state is a functioning democracy with a willingness and the apparatus necessary to provide a measure of protection to its citizens.

paragraphs.summary: The panel states refugee protection is surrogate and claimant must seek state protection or claim usually fails in functioning democracies.

propositions.text: Claimant's burden to prove state protection failure increases with state's democracy level.
propositions.quote: The claimant's burden of proof is directly proportional to the level of democracy in the state in question: the more democratic the state's institutions, the more the claimant must have done to exhaust all courses of action open to them.

propositions.text: In functioning democracies, claimant must exhaust all reasonable protection steps before claiming refugee status.
propositions.quote: In a functioning democracy, a claimant will have a heavy burden when attempting to show that they should not have been required to exhaust all of the recourses available to them domestically before claiming refugee status.

propositions.text: Claimant must show all reasonable steps taken considering country context and interactions with authorities.
propositions.quote: The claimant must do more than merely show that he or she went to see members of the police force and that those efforts were unsuccessful. A claimant must show that they have taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken and the claimant's interactions with the authorities.

propositions.text: Local failures do not mean state fails unless part of broader pattern of inability or refusal to protect.
propositions.quote: Local failures by authorities to provide protection do not mean that the state as a whole fails to protect its citizens, unless the failures form part of a broader pattern of the state's inability or refusal to provide protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel explains claimant's heavy burden to exhaust protection steps in functioning democracies and local failures don't prove state failure.

propositions.text: The claimant has not provided clear and convincing evidence that state protection in Mexico is inadequate on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: In view of these principles, the panel finds that the claimant has not provided clear and convincing evidence, that on a balance of probabilities, state protection in Mexico is inadequate.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he witnessed his neighbour's kidnapping and later learned neighbour's body was found.
propositions.quote: He testified that he witnessed his neighbour being dragged from his home and placed into a pick-up truck by three men. On XXXXX, 2008, from the newspaper, he later learned that bodies were found in different parts of the cities and one of those bodies was his neighbour's who he had witnessed being dragged from his home on XXXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he called an anonymous emergency call service to report the incident he witnessed.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that on XXXXX, 2008 he called the emergency call service which is set up for citizens to anonymously call and report crimes they may have witnessed. He reported the incident he had witnessed.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant failed to prove state protection inadequate; claimant reported neighbour's kidnapping anonymously.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he was threatened by a kidnapper at his door, received a threatening note, but did not report it to police.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that on XXXXX 2008, someone who he recognized as one of the men who had dragged away his neighbour was at his door knocking. He did not open the door but overheard the man talking on his cell-phone that he was going to kill the claimant. The man also slid a note under the claimant's door which stated that they already knew who the claimant was and he should not open his mouth about anything he had heard or seen or he would be killed. The note was signed XXXXX XXXXX The claimant did not report the incident to the police.

propositions.text: The claimant fled his job and belongings to another city but was found; he threw away the threatening note.
propositions.quote: Instead, he said he left his job, his belongings and fled to XXXXX, XXXXX, where he found a new job. He also said he threw away the note.

propositions.text: The claimant had a police friend but did not report the threat to him, only mentioned it informally; he said friend could not help much.
propositions.quote: However, the claimant testified that he had a friend who was a sergeant in the municipal police force. The claimant was asked why he did not report the incident to his police friend. He said because his friend could not help him too much. However, the claimant testified that he did mention the incident to this police friend in an informal way and he told him to watch himself for these were heavy duty guys and dangerous.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant's omission of the police friend conversation in his narrative undermines his credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel believes if he had had that conversation with a police officer who told him to be careful because the men who threatened him are dangerous, he would have included it in his narrative. The panel notes that the claimant is represented by counsel and he, with the help of counsel, had previously amended his narrative. Therefore, the panel finds that this omission undermines the claimant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant did not report threats to police or police friend and omission of conversation undermines credibility.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the claimant's testimony about the threatening note slid under his door.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the claimant's testimony that he was threatened that he would be killed by drug gangsters that was contained in a written note that was slid under his door, the panel does not believe.

propositions.text: The claimant said he threw away the note because he was frightened and did not think he would come to Canada.
propositions.quote: He was asked what he did with the note, and he said he threw it away. Asked why he threw the note away, the claimant said that he got so frightened he started to think about the problems and how to get out of them. So he was asked again, why did he throw the note away. At that point the claimant said he did not think he would need it, as he did not think he would be coming to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves claimant's testimony about the threatening note and notes he threw it away fearing problems.

propositions.text: The claimant was making up the story about the alleged note as he went along.
propositions.quote: The panel believes that the claimant was making up the story as he went along in respect to the alleged note.

propositions.text: The claimant's initial response about the note was evasive, vague and confusing.
propositions.quote: The panel finds the claimant's answer evasive, vague and confusing

propositions.text: On a balance of probability, there is no threatening note; it is a fabrication to bolster his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: on a balance of probability there is no threatening note. The note is a fabrication to bolster his claim for refugee status.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant fabricated the threatening note and gave evasive answers about it.

propositions.text: The claimant's claim is based on the alleged threatening note which is central to his allegation.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that the foundation of the claimant's claim is based on the threatening note he alleged he received.

propositions.text: The panel must be satisfied that evidence is probably so, not just possibly so.
propositions.quote: it has an obligation to be satisfied that the evidence it relies on is probably so, not possibly so.

propositions.text: There is no persuasive evidence that the claimant's allegations are probably so, especially lacking corroborative documents like the note.
propositions.quote: The panel finds no persuasive evidence before it that the claimant's allegations are probably so, and not possibly so, especially in the absence of corroborative documents, such as the note

propositions.text: Lack of documentary corroboration is a valid consideration in assessing credibility when the story is implausible or lacks credibility.
propositions.quote: this panel finds a lack of documentary corroboration to be a valid consideration in assessing the claimant's credibility

propositions.text: It is reasonable to attach great importance to documentation supporting allegations.
propositions.quote: It is therefore reasonable for the panel to attach great importance to documentation which would have supported the allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no persuasive evidence or corroboration for the claimant's allegations, which rely on the threatening note.

propositions.text: The panel is entitled to rely on documentary evidence over claimant's testimony, even if claimant is credible.
propositions.quote: The panel reminds itself that it is entitled to rely on documentary evidence in preference to the testimony provided by the claimant, even if it finds the claimant trustworthy and credible.

propositions.text: The Federal Court cautions the panel in relying on documentary evidence over testimony.
propositions.quote: the panel also notes the caution that the Federal Court has provided to the panel in taking this approach.

paragraphs.summary: The panel can prefer documentary evidence over testimony but must heed Federal Court caution.

propositions.text: Claimant must show he took all reasonable steps to seek state protection considering country context and interactions with authorities.
propositions.quote: the claimant must show that he has taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken and his interactions with the authorities.

propositions.text: The claimant made no efforts to approach state protection and his explanation for not doing so was not compelling.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that he made absolutely no efforts to approach the state for protection; and finds that his explanation for not taking all reasonable steps to seek state protection was not compelling

propositions.text: Failure to pursue state protection without compelling explanation is usually fatal to refugee claim in functioning democracies.
propositions.quote: a failure to pursue state protection opportunities within the home state will usually be fatal to a refugee claim, at least where the state is a functioning democracy

propositions.text: There is no persuasive evidence that Mexico is a failed state.
propositions.quote: There is no persuasive evidence before it that Mexico is a failed state.

propositions.text: Doubting state protection effectiveness without testing it does not rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: doubting the effectiveness of the protection offered by the state when the claimant has not really tested it does not rebut the existence of a presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant made no effort to seek state protection and Mexico is not a failed state, so presumption of protection stands.

propositions.text: Adequacy of state protection cannot rest on claimant's subjective fear.
propositions.quote: the adequacy of state protection cannot rest on the subjective fear of the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant cannot rebut presumption of state protection by subjective reluctance to engage state.
propositions.quote: A claimant cannot rebut the presumption of state protection in a functioning democracy by asserting only a subjective reluctance to engage the state

paragraphs.summary: Federal Court rules claimant's subjective fear cannot rebut presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Fleeing before police investigate does not mean lack of state protection.
propositions.quote: a claimant's decision to flee before police have had an opportunity to properly respond to and investigate a transgression did not amount to a lack of state protection.

propositions.text: No information suggests police would not investigate if claimant reported and followed up.
propositions.quote: there is no information to suggest that police would not make genuine and earnest efforts to investigate the claimant's allegations and apprehend the perpetrators if the claimant had reported the incidents to the police and in the case of the one incident the police was made aware of, if the claimant had followed up.

propositions.text: Claimant's leaving Mexico may have delayed or stymied investigation as he was a key witness.
propositions.quote: The claimant's choice to leave Mexico may have resulted in the investigation being delayed or stymied, given that he, as the victim, was a key witness.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds fleeing before police investigation does not negate state protection; claimant's leaving may have hindered investigation.

propositions.text: Claimant did not approach any other authorities and simply left Mexico.
propositions.quote: the claimant did not approach any other authorities; he simply left Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant did not seek help from other authorities and left Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant said police in Mexico are corrupt and loyal to drug traffickers.
propositions.quote: The claimant responded that the police in Mexico are corrupt. For example, police offers' loyalty is divided among different groups of drug traffickers.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's views on state protection are not objectively well-founded and contradict documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel found the claimant's responses regarding the effectiveness of state protection to be not objectively well-founded since they were largely unsubstantiated and contradict the documentary evidence

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges police corruption but panel finds his views unsubstantiated and contradict documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant believes police forces are involved with drug dealers and cannot identify honest officers, based on media.
propositions.quote: He said that as far as he is aware the police forces in Mexico are involved with drug dealers and he cannot guess which police officer is honest. The claimant based his belief on what he has gathered from the media.

propositions.text: Claimant said Human Rights Commission has little influence and won't investigate cases due to threats.
propositions.quote: When he was asked about the Human Rights Commission, he said that they did not have a big influence in Mexico. Asked why they don't have a big influence, he said they will not investigate cases because they too can be threatened.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's belief in police corruption and ineffective Human Rights Commission is based on media and unsubstantiated.

propositions.text: Claimant does not trust any police level in Mexico due to widespread corruption.
propositions.quote: The claimant responded that he does not trust any level of police in Mexico because the majority of the police in Mexico are corrupt.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's views on state protection not objectively well-founded and contradict documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel found the claimant's responses regarding the effectiveness of state protection to be not objectively well-founded since they were largely unsubstantiated and contradict the documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Documentation shows corruption and inefficiency remain issues but Mexico is making serious efforts to rectify them.
propositions.quote: there is information in the documentation to indicate that inefficiency, bribery and corruption remain issues in Mexican security forces at all levels... Mexico candidly acknowledges its past problems and is making serious efforts to rectify the corruption and impunity that exists.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant distrusts police due to corruption; panel finds documentation shows issues but Mexico is addressing them.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Mexico is a functioning democracy with free elections and independent judiciary.
propositions.quote: Mexico is a functioning democracy, and there are free and fair elections. There is a relatively independent and impartial judiciary.

propositions.text: Mexico controls its territory with functioning security forces; no evidence of complete breakdown.
propositions.quote: Mexico is in effective control of its territory and has in place a functioning security force... There is nothing in the documentary evidence before the Board to suggest that Mexico is in a state of complete breakdown.

paragraphs.summary: Documentary evidence shows Mexico is a functioning democracy with effective control and security forces.

propositions.text: Mexico has had difficulties with criminality and corruption but is making serious efforts to address them.
propositions.quote: Mexico has had some difficulties... but the preponderance of the objective evidence... suggests... there is an adequate state protection in Mexico... Mexico is making serious efforts to address the problem of criminality

propositions.text: Police corruption and deficiencies exist but are not systemic and are being addressed by the state.
propositions.quote: Police corruption and deficiencies... are not systemic. The panel is of the view... that... the issues of corruption and deficiencies are being addressed by the state of Mexico.

propositions.text: Low pay and lack of resources hinder police performance and anti-corruption efforts.
propositions.quote: Corruption and inefficiency plague the Mexican police. In addition, low pay and lack of resources have hindered efforts at improving police performance, battling corruption, and professionalizing the forces.

propositions.text: Recent polls show low public confidence in police; government has made reducing corruption a key goal with international recognition.
propositions.quote: In more recent nationwide polls, only 12 percent of the population has expressed confidence in the police. In response... President Fox made reducing public corruption a key goal... and he gained international recognition for his efforts.

paragraphs.summary: Mexico faces police corruption but is actively addressing it; public confidence is low but government efforts recognized.

propositions.text: Mexican government introduced reforms including new police forces and restructuring to combat crime and corruption.
propositions.quote: The Mexican government has introduced a number of significant reforms in its security forces to combat crime over the past number of years...

propositions.text: Federal Investigative Police replaced corrupt Federal Judicial Police; efforts ongoing to professionalize AFI.
propositions.quote: the Federal Investigative Police (AFI) recently established... replaced the notoriously corrupt Federal Judicial Police (PJF). Efforts to develop the AFI into a professional, corruption-free force... are ongoing.

propositions.text: Federal Preventive Police created in 1999 to prevent and combat crime, assuming greater authority over time.
propositions.quote: The Federal Preventive Police (PFP) was created in 1999 ... to prevent and combat crime throughout the country... has been assuming greater authority in stages over time

propositions.text: Public Security Secretariat of Federal District manages large police force in Mexico City with efforts to improve accountability and effectiveness.
propositions.quote: The Public Security Secretariat of the federal District (SSP-DF)... manages a combined force of over 90,000 officers... efforts to increase accountability and improve police effectiveness.

propositions.text: Mexico City Mayor hired Rudy Giuliani as consultant to SSP-DF in 2002 to improve police effectiveness.
propositions.quote: Mexico City Mayor Andrés Obrador's decision in 2002 to contract former New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani as a consultant to the SSP-DF.

paragraphs.summary: Mexico has reformed police forces and hired consultants to improve effectiveness and combat corruption.

propositions.text: Mexico created agencies to combat crime, drug cartels, and organized crime including UEDO, FEADS, and SIEDO.
propositions.quote: Mexico created a number of agencies to combat crime, the drug cartels and organized crime: First, the PGR's Special Anti-Organized Crime Unit (UEDO)... Second... Office of the Special Prosecutor for Crimes against Health (FEADS)... Third... Office of the Deputy Attorney for Special Investigation of Organized Crime (SIEDO)

propositions.text: SIEDO has six special units investigating specific crimes including drug trafficking, terrorism, money laundering, human trafficking, kidnappings, and theft.
propositions.quote: SIEDO contains six special units for investigating specific types of crimes: crimes against public health; terrorism and arms trafficking; money laundering and counterfeiting; human trafficking in minors, organs, and undocumented people; kidnappings; and robber and other theft.

propositions.text: Mexican policing institutions reorganize rationally to respond effectively to specific crime problems.
propositions.quote: The special offices of the PGR demonstrate the general rule that Mexican policing institutions try to reorganize themselves in a rational way to respond effectively to specific crime problems.

paragraphs.summary: Mexico created specialized agencies and units to combat organized crime and drug trafficking effectively.

propositions.text: Persons facing police misconduct can ask Secretariat of Public Administration, Program Against Impunity, or Attorney General to investigate.
propositions.quote: persons who face police misconduct, inefficiency or corruption can ask the Secretariat of the Public Administration (SFP), the Program Against Impunity, or the Office of the Attorney General (PGR) to investigate federal and state police failures or misconduct.

paragraphs.summary: Victims of police misconduct can request investigations from various Mexican authorities.

propositions.text: Efforts to ensure police effectiveness and purge corruption include investigations, complaints monitoring, and a 24-hour hotline.
propositions.quote: efforts to ensure police effectiveness and purge corruption include investigations by the Secretary of Public Security, complaints monitored by the Inspector General, and a 24-hour hotline to report corrupt officials.

paragraphs.summary: Mexico has mechanisms like investigations and hotlines to combat police corruption.

propositions.text: Security forces instituted new recruiting, drug testing, incentives, education, and sanctions against corrupt officers.
propositions.quote: security forces have instituted new recruiting procedures, drug testing, economic incentives, education and certification of officers, with sanctions levied against ineffective or corrupt officers

propositions.text: New laws have resulted in imprisonment sentences for corrupt officials, having a marked effect.
propositions.quote: new government laws attacking corruption and bribery have resulted in sentences of five to 10 years' imprisonment for convicted officials, which have reportedly had a marked effect.

paragraphs.summary: Mexico has implemented reforms and laws to punish corrupt police officers effectively.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to rebut presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence.
propositions.quote: the claimant... has failed to rebut the presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence

propositions.text: Claimant did not take all reasonable steps to avail himself of state protection before claiming refugee protection.
propositions.quote: the claimant did not take all reasonable steps in the circumstances to avail himself of that protection before making a claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: Panel is not persuaded Mexico would not provide reasonable state protection if claimant sought it.
propositions.quote: the panel is not persuaded that the state of Mexico would not be reasonably forthcoming with state protection, should the claimant seek it.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant failed to rebut presumption of state protection and did not seek it before claiming refugee status.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection as state protection is available.
propositions.quote: the panel finds that that the claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection... as state protection is available to him.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant is not a refugee or protected person because state protection is available.

propositions.text: The Refugee Protection Division rejects the claimant's claim as he is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. The Refugee Protection Division therefore rejects his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim.
